name: Shensong Yangxin (Chinese herbal medicine)
short: In a 12-month placebo-controlled trial in 920 people after ablation for atrial fibrillation, serious adverse events did not differ; meta-analyses found no excess of adverse events.
text: In a 12-month multicentre, placebo-controlled trial in 920 people in China who had catheter ablation for persistent atrial fibrillation, there was no significant difference in the incidence of serious adverse events between Shensong Yangxin capsules taken by mouth and placebo; the abstract does not describe which events occurred. A 2026 meta-analysis of 9 randomized trials (2199 patients) of the capsules added to anti-arrhythmic drugs after ablation found no statistically significant difference in adverse events between the capsule and control groups, and its authors caution that extrapolation to Western populations requires caution. A 2025 meta-analysis of 10 randomized trials (1,713 patients with persistent atrial fibrillation) reported fewer adverse reactions when the capsules were combined with conventional treatments than with conventional treatments alone (relative risk 0.54); the abstract states that the certainty of evidence was graded as moderate to low, without saying for which outcomes. The abstracts do not say whether the 920-person trial is among the trials either meta-analysis pooled. These data come mainly from Chinese trials in which the capsules were added to standard treatment, and the abstracts do not list the formula's herbs. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
